metadata.title: What It Had to Guess
metadata.audience: A hiring manager or engineer deciding whether the author can tell a verified claim from an unverified one
metadata.greeting_note: The assignment requires narrating as myself and forbids the instructor's name, persona or credit line, so the toolkit's claude-liam persona, IN-FOR-BEAR LAW and the @NikBearBrown outro lock are deliberately not used. The voice is synthetic and B00 says so in its first breath.
metadata.source: Pepper — The Personal AI Prompter, v0.3 (pepper-v0.3.zip): CHANGES.md, pepper-extension/README.md, PRIVACY.md, manifest.json, lib/core.js, pepper-tests/README.md, docs/LIVE-TEST-PROTOCOL.md. Alternatives read on their own pages, 10 Oct 2026: help.openai.com (ChatGPT Custom Instructions) and aiprm.com.
metadata.one_idea: A prompt is only as good as the context behind it, and the cost of missing context scales with how much the tool is allowed to do. Pepper's distinguishing move is that it shows you what it had to guess instead of inventing it — and the project is to verify, on the live sites, the one link its tests cannot see.
metadata.tts_note: Every figure is written as words. 'Uh-mohg Muddoor' is a phonetic respelling used in narration_text ONLY: the literal spelling 'Maddur' phonemizes to /mˈædjʊɹ/ ('MAD-yoor'), heard back by ASR as 'Madger'. The respelling gives /ˈʌmˈoʊɡ mˈʌdɔːɹ/. Never on screen. 'AIPRM' is never spoken (no letter-by-letter sequences); it appears on screen only.
metadata.voice_note: am_puck — the voice chosen by spectral-centroid measurement for the previous reel (2883 Hz vs am_onyx 1748 Hz) and already round-tripped clean through ASR. Reused because it has no known defects.
metadata.headroom_note: Uniform −3.00 dB applied to every beat so the loudest peak sits at about −3 dBFS (the loudest beat was +0.0 dBFS). B06, B07 and B09 were regenerated afterwards with hold tails and given the same fixed −3.00 dB, so relative loudness is unchanged. Durations re-measured after every pass.
